title: Babies Have No Bony Kneecaps (Until Age 3) 🦵
description:
Why are babies born without bony kneecaps? A baby's kneecap starts as soft cartilage and only begins turning to bone between about ages 3 and 6, fusing into one solid kneecap by the early teens.

Sources:
https://www.healthline.com/health/do-babies-have-kneecaps
https://radiopaedia.org/articles/24732

Animated in the Flat-Vector Science style.
pinned_comment: Be honest: did you know you were born without bony kneecaps? 🦵
topic: Why are babies born without hard kneecaps?
script: Your kneecaps were soft until you were about three. Babies don't have bony kneecaps at all. Each knee has a soft disc of cartilage instead, the same bendy stuff in the tip of your nose. So why start soft? First, there's birth itself. A hard kneecap would make that tight squeeze riskier. Then comes crawling. Knees hit the floor again and again, and soft cartilage handles that better than bone. Then somewhere between ages three and six, tiny islands of bone pop up inside the cartilage. They grow, they spread, and by your early teens they've fused into one solid kneecap. And honestly, it's kind of a weird bone. It's the biggest bone in your body that grows right inside a tendon. That's why a toddler's knees are still so squishy. So be honest. Did you know you were born without kneecaps?
key_facts: Babies are born with a kneecap made of cartilage, not bone (Healthline)
Patella ossification centers appear between about 3 and 6 years (Radiopaedia; Healthline says 2-6)
Several pieces harden and fuse into one bone by about age 10-12 / puberty
A rigid kneecap could make birth harder; cartilage handles crawling and learning to walk better (Healthline)
The patella is the largest sesamoid bone, embedded in the quadriceps tendon (Radiopaedia)
